approvalTitle: requirements.md: converting the RDF diagrams to DISL and FBL
content:
# Requirements Document

## Introduction

The user's request, verbatim (2026-10-09):

> Create spec workflow MCP specifications. One specification for converting one of the standalone diagram tools to FBL and DISL. i.e. analyse the current implementation, define the DISL and FBL and then write the specification on the refactoring., also focus on finding issues and aspects where the DISL and FBL languages do not yet cover everything.

This is one of the fifteen specifications that reading gives (the series and the survey behind it are in `causal-loop-disl-fbl`, *Introduction*). It converts the **RDF** module (`src/diagrams/rdf/`, Turtle `.ttl` and N-Triples `.nt`), which is four tool types over one body: the **RDF graph** (`w3c/rdf`), the **OWL ontology** (`w3c/owl`), the **SHACL shapes** (`w3c/shacl`) and the **SKOS concept scheme** (`w3c/skos`). One specification covers the module, because the four share one tokenizer, one parser, one writer, one store and one history, and none can be converted without the others.

**This tool is on neither language, and its format is one FBL expects to stay a plugin.** FBL 11.5 lists Turtle and N-Triples first among "the formats expected to stay plugins": "Terms span tokens, prefixes compress IRIs, and one IRI yields several elements; the projection is code." So the body is not bound by rules. `RdfTokenizer` and `RdfParser` become the plugin's `read`, `RdfWriter` and `ShaclWriter` become its `plan`, and everything else FBL declares (routing, the four readings, the registration, the templates, history, drift and saving) is done by the host. **The findings of part B are therefore about the plugin contract**, and the largest of them is that the contract hands `plan` one model change at a time while this module's edits are not shaped that way.

**What "converted" means here** is what it means in `causal-loop-disl-fbl`: toolbox, context menus, property rows, findings and refusals derived from bundled DISL definitions, the body read and written through the FBL binding, and module code only for what neither language can state. Nothing a user sees or a file holds changes unless this document names the change and the user has ruled on it.

## What was measured

Read on 2026-10-09: the module at `develop` `9a646009`; in etalii-adp/etalii.adp at `develop` `da64ff0` the four drafts `definitions/diagrams/w3c-rdf.dis`, `w3c-owl.dis`, `w3c-shacl.dis` and `w3c-skos.dis` with their `.md` companions, the DISL specification's own example `specifications/disl/rdf-graph.dis`, the binding `specifications/fbl/w3c-turtle.fbl`, the DISL specification (0.3 draft) and the FBL specification (0.2 draft); and the two libraries here.

| Thing | State |
| --- | --- |
| The module's backend | 12,770 lines of C# in 121 files. `RdfTokenizer` (383 lines) and `RdfParser` (603) read; `RdfWriter` (601) and `ShaclWriter` (467) write; four projections (`RdfProjection` 225, `OwlProjection` 460, `ShaclProjection` 612, `SkosProjection` 349) turn triples into drawn elements; four validators give 23 finding codes; the providers hold 9 toolbox ids, 22 action ids and 17 property ids. 44 test files, 7,825 lines, nine fixtures. |
| The module's client | 2,471 lines without tests: four hand-written canvases (`RdfCanvas`, `OwlCanvas`, `ShaclCanvas`, `SkosCanvas`). |
| The DISL definitions | Four drafts in etalii.adp of 516, 825, 608 and 588 lines, **all written against DISL 0.1**, each declaring `persistence.format` as `plugin:net.etalii.adp.w3c.turtle`. A fifth description, `rdf-graph.dis` (632 lines, DISL 0.2), is the DISL specification's worked example of derived elements. None is bundled here: the module has no `definition/` folder. |
| The FBL binding | Exists as an example, 35 lines, `"fbl": "0.1"`, reader `net.etalii.adp.w3c.turtle`, vendored unchanged in `EtAlii.Adp.Specification.Fbl.Tests/Conformance/`. No plugin with that id exists; the library's tests open it with a fake one. |
| The real-file check | `Registrations.Tests` routes the 33 `.ttl` and `.nt` files under `src/` to the binding and checks that each sibling registration's `suggest` matches its body. `ModuleCrossCheck.Tests` does not cover the module, and `RealFiles/divergences.json` has no entry for it. |
| Registrations | 25 under `src/` name one of the four origins (10, 4, 6 and 5). Seven hold a `layout:` block, 48 positions in all, every key of the shape `res:` followed by a full IRI. Five carry a `language:` header. |
| A parity transcript | None. |

**How each finding is known:** *recorded* is a test, an entry of the vendored fixtures, a comment in the module's code or a sentence of the companion notes that says so; *measured* is a search whose command is in *Sources*; *read* is a reading of code against specification text, not run. Nothing was built or run. Requirement 1 turns every *read* finding into a fixture first.

## Findings

The three kinds are those of `causal-loop-disl-fbl`: a **definition defect** is repaired in a definition or the binding, a **runtime gap** in this repository's libraries, a **language gap** in etalii-adp/etalii.adp.

### A. The DISL definitions against the module

| # | Finding | Kind | Known |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A1 | All four drafts are DISL 0.1. The client refuses anything but 0.3. Each is rewritten at 0.3 before it can be bundled. | Definition defect | Measured |
| A2 | **Three descriptions of the RDF graph disagree about where the elements come from.** The 0.1 draft hands the whole projection to the plugin. `rdf-graph.dis` stores `Triple` and `Base` elements and derives cards, bands and statements from them in CEL, declares no `format` and no `binding`, and declares the plugin as providing `action` and `celFunctions` only. The binding names the same plugin as its reader, which FBL 11.1 requires to be declared with `provides: ["persistenceFormat"]`. | Definition defect, and the choice is Q2 | Read |
| A3 | The four companions list as inexpressible what DISL 0.2 and 0.3 have since answered: nodes derived from other elements (4.11, whose own example is "an RDF resource card is every triple sharing a subject", one SKOS edge merged from `broader` and `narrower`, and an OWL IRI that is both a class and an individual); ids that must never be stored (`ephemeral` with a `reason`, 11.5.3); ids from IRIs and from triples with a repeat counter (`derived`, 11.5.2); findings on lines and a parse failure as the only finding (`std.unparseable` given the code `rdf.unparseable`, 8.6); a budget that cuts, shows a notice and withholds edits (3.2.1); a counted menu label (4.11.4); a recursive text function with a depth cap (3.4); a confirming button's label (`submitLabel`, 7.5); and types shared by several specifications (`imports`, 3.3). | Definition defect | Read |
| A4 | **What of each tool type is derivable has only been written down for one of the four.** For the RDF graph, `rdf-graph.dis` derives cards, blank cards, type bands, rows and statements. For OWL (classification of every IRI, punning with `ind:` beside `res:`, the `thing:` and `dt:` anchors that stand for a missing domain or range and have no triple of their own, and the expression text of `ExpressionRenderer`), for SHACL (shapes by declaration or by use, rows and target chips that are list items and not elements, the path syntax) and for SKOS (merged hierarchy edges, the label chosen by language) no 0.3 definition exists, and whether each fits in CEL within `limits.celCost` is not known. | To establish per reading in design (Requirement 4.5) | Read |
| A5 | The standalone DISL runtime does not compute derived node types: `DislModelBuilder` computes derived ids and derived relations only. It implements no budget, refuses a specification that declares `imports` ("This runtime does not resolve imports"), and `DislCelLibrary` has none of `diagram.cycles`, `reachable` and `inCycle`, which `owl.subclass-cycle` and `skos.hierarchy-cycle` need. | Runtime gap | Measured |
| A6 | The drafts give no wire ids. The module's toolbox, action and property ids, its finding codes and its element ids are what the client and every stored registration use. | Language gap, already ruled: wire ids stay an `x-` block (Peter, 2026-10-06). Each definition gets its own: `x-rdf`, `x-owl`, `x-shacl`, `x-skos`. | Read |
| A7 | **One reading's entries appear under another.** One action provider and one property provider answer for all four origins. A file opened as `w3c/rdf` that asserts an `owl:Ontology` is offered the four OWL add entries and "Subclass of"; `SkosActions` and `SkosProperties` carry no origin check, so a resource typed as a concept gets the scheme reading's entries and grid under any reading; SHACL's answer only for their own origin. A remark in `RdfSelection.cs` says the opposite was intended. Four definitions give each reading its own menus, so deriving them removes the leak. | Behaviour change to rule on (Q4) | Recorded (`w3c-rdf.md`, section 6 and difference 18) |
| A8 | **The SKOS `language` header has no reader.** FBL lets a binding declare a registration header and the binding declares this one. The plugin's `read` receives the body's bytes and the binding's `args`, and no CEL context of DISL 12.3 reads a registration. The label the scheme reading draws depends on that header. | Language gap | Measured |
| A9 | `skos.misplaced-header` reports a `language:` line written above `body:`, which today severs the pairing. FBL 8.1 reads headers in any order, so the hazard and the finding both go. The module also reads `language:de` without a space, matches the key without regard to case, lowercases the value and scans eight lines; FBL splits a header at the first colon followed by a space. | Behaviour change to rule on (Q3) | Read |
| A10 | The id rules and the `types` attribute of `rdf-graph.dis` filter every triple once per triple, so reading is quadratic in the number of triples. The largest examples are 11,022 and 8,260 lines. DISL has no grouping function that would make them linear. | To settle by measurement; a language gap if it fails | Read |
| A11 | The type-band layout, the OWL satellite placement, the SKOS and SHACL layouts, the viewport filter and the `.proto` payloads stay code. Resolving a typed term against the file's prefixes stays a plugin CEL function (13.1.1). Neither is a gap: DISL names layouts for a plugin (D.2, open question 9) and has no streaming model on purpose. | None | Read |

### B. The binding and the plugin contract against the module's reader and writers

| # | Finding | Kind | Known |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B1 | **`plan` receives one model change; the module's edits are several that only make sense together.** Removing a resource removes every triple that names it, reparsing between each. Removing a shape sweeps the blank subtrees written inside it. A new property row is one `sh:property [ … ]` block holding several triples on a blank node that is created and never addressed. Planned one at a time against the same bytes, the removal of two pairs of one statement each claims the same `;`, the removal of all pairs leaves a subject and a `.`, and the block's triples cannot be written as a block. `PluginBody.Order` throws on overlapping splices, and `PluginBody.Change` applies one change as one history entry, so one gesture would be several undo steps. | Language gap (FBL 11.2), with a runtime gap behind it | Read |
| B2 | **Renaming a term and declaring a prefix are not the adding, setting or removing of one stored element.** `RenameTerm` rewrites every token that names the IRI, in subject, predicate, object and datatype position, bracketed or prefixed under the prefixes in force at that point. `rdf-graph.dis` routes both to a plugin `action`. FBL 11.4 says a plugin must not write files, and neither specification says how an action hands the host splices for its history. | Language gap (FBL 11.2 and DISL 9, 13.1) | Read |
| B3 | **One token holds a value of several elements.** A subject is written once for every pair of a `;` list and a predicate once for every object of a `,` list. FBL 3.3 binds a writable value to exactly one place and 11.2 asks `read` for "the source span of the entry and of every writable value". The parser stamps one statement range on every triple of a statement, and a triple inside an inline blank property list carries the enclosing statement's range. | Language gap | Recorded (the remarks on `RemoveTripleAnchored`) |
| B4 | **Adding a pair to an existing statement changes its terminator.** `AddTriple` replaces the `.` by `;` in place and writes the pair on a new line. None of the eleven operations of FBL 6.1 names the replacement of a separator, and 11.4 requires a plugin to name its operations truthfully. A single insertion before the `.` gives the same bytes only when nothing follows the `.` on its line; a trailing comment would move down a line. | Language gap, minor | Read |
| B5 | **The spans are in another unit.** The parser records UTF-16 offsets into `LineDocument.Text` and line ranges; a splice is a range of UTF-8 bytes counted with a byte-order mark. `examples/w3c-turtle/example-1.ttl` holds a Cyrillic literal, so the two differ in a shipped file. No fixture starts with a byte-order mark, and neither `RdfTokenizer` nor `LineDocument` mentions one. | Conversion work, with fixtures | Measured |
| B6 | **What an edit writes, where the writer and FBL 6.3 differ.** A new line takes the document's dominant ending (LF only when LF lines outnumber CRLF lines); FBL takes the ending of the line the insertion point is on. Replacing a literal rewrites the whole token as a short double-quoted string, so `'''…'''` and an explicit `^^xsd:string` are lost when only the language changes. A new prefix is always written `@prefix`, in a file that uses `PREFIX` too. A removal trims the whitespace it strands and deletes a line left holding only whitespace, and does not take the comment lines above a statement. | Behaviour change to rule on (Q1) | Read; the literal and the prefix form are recorded in `w3c-rdf.md` |
| B7 | **An N-Triples file is written as Turtle.** Adding a triple to a subject that already has one writes `;`, which N-Triples does not have. The plugin cannot do better under the contract either: `read` and `plan` receive bytes, and for a file body no name or extension. | Module defect, to fix on purpose with its own guard; and a language gap | Recorded (`w3c-rdf.md`, section 2) |
| B8 | **The templates.** The binding's `template.text` declares an unused `rdf:` prefix and states one `rdfs:label`; `RdfDocumentFactory` writes `a ex:Resource ;` and the label on a second line. The binding has `byOrigin` for `w3c/skos` only; `OwlDocumentFactory` and `ShaclDocumentFactory` have their own starters. `{key}` replaces `-` by `_` and prefixes `_` before a leading digit; the factories' `LocalOf` keeps `-` and does neither. `Templates.Tests` holds the binding's text. | Definition defect | Recorded |
| B9 | **A bare file and a missing file.** The binding says `createOnFirstPlacement: true`; the four sessions refuse a move with "This diagram was opened without a registration, so there is nowhere to store a position. Register the file to arrange it." A body that does not exist opens empty and the first save creates it; FBL 8.2 opens it with `fbl.missing-body` and writes nothing. | Behaviour change to rule on (Q3) | Read |
| B10 | **Stale and renamed positions.** Nothing prunes a stale layout entry, and a rename leaves the old `res:` position behind. FBL 8.5 removes a stale entry at the next write, and DISL 11.5.2 rewrites view keys when a derived id changes. | Behaviour change to rule on (Q3) | Recorded (`w3c-rdf.md`, section 3) |
| B11 | **The stored ids read as they are.** Every stored key is `res:` and a full IRI, which FBL 8.1 reads whole because the key ends at the last colon followed by a space and an IRI holds no space. Numbers are written to three decimals by both. `blank:` and the ordinal, and OWL's `expr:` ids, are refused a position today with two sentences that become the `reason` of an `ephemeral` rule. A repeated triple's `\|n` suffix is DISL's repeat counter. | None | Measured |
| B12 | **Offering readings.** The binding's `suggest` strings are those of `Diagram.cs`, and only `w3c/rdf` is `bare`, as today. FBL tests the first 64 KiB of a body. `claims.origins` lists rdf, owl, shacl, skos; `Diagram.Definitions` lists rdf, owl, skos, shacl, so the offered order differs. | Definition defect, minor | Recorded (`Registrations.Tests`, `Routing.Tests`) |
| B13 | **Undo.** Every command's inverse is a whole-document snapshot and its redo re-runs the command. The host of FBL 7 undoes by inverse splices and refuses on drift with a sentence of its own. The bytes are the same; the refusal is new. | Behaviour change, accepted with the host | Read |
| B14 | **Sentences of the unreadable body.** The module says "This file does not parse, so nothing can be edited until it is fixed."; `PluginBody` says "The file could not be read, so it is never written." | Runtime gap (the sentence must be the tool's) | Read |
| B15 | **Findings are shared by every reading of an open body** (FBL 9.1). Only the five `rdf.*` findings may come from `read`; the eighteen of the three siblings are each definition's constraints. `OwlValidator` already delegates the file-level rules, so this matches. | None | Read |

### C. Language gaps, as they would be reported to etalii-adp/etalii.adp

1. **FBL: `plan` for a whole transaction** (B1). Candidate: `plan` receives the ordered list of a transaction's changes and delivers one set of splices, so a plugin can write a group as one construct and resolve changes that touch one statement.
2. **FBL and DISL: an edit that is not a change of one element** (B2). Candidate: a plugin action that delivers splices under the rules of FBL 11.4, applied and recorded by the host as one edit; or a `rename` change that names a value and every place it is written.
3. **FBL: a writable value shared by several elements** (B3). Section 3.3 and the `read` contract assume one place per value per element.
4. **FBL: a splice operation for a separator or terminator** (B4), or the statement that a plugin's operation names are its own.
5. **FBL: what `read` and `plan` are told about the document** (B7, A8): the body's name, and the registration's declared headers. **DISL: a registration header readable in CEL** (A8).
6. **DISL: a grouping function** (A10), if the measurement shows the derived readings exceed the cost limit on the examples.
7. **DISL: entries of one specification offered under another reading of the same body** (A7), only if the user rules that the leak is kept.

These are candidates. Requirement 10 says they are recorded with their evidence and reported, and never worked around silently.

## Open questions

Each is put to the user as a selection. The option marked **(default)** is what this document is written against.

| # | Question | Options | Criteria affected |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Q1 | Where today's writer and FBL's new-text rules write different bytes (finding B6), what is written? | **(default) Today's bytes, except the line ending**, which follows FBL 6.3 because 11.4 makes it a MUST and it differs only in a file of mixed endings; the transcript's hunks for that one fixture are regenerated and reviewed. · **FBL's smaller change everywhere it applies**: a literal keeps its quoting and its datatype spelling, a prefix follows the file's own form. · Other. | 5.3, 1.4 |
| Q2 | What does the plugin's `read` deliver (finding A2)? | **(default) Triples, prefixes and the base as stored elements**, and each reading derives its drawn elements in DISL, as DISL 4.11 and `rdf-graph.dis` describe; one model serves four readings, as FBL 9.1 requires. · **Each reading's drawn elements**, computed by the module's four projections: no CEL risk, and it needs `read` to be told the reading, which FBL does not allow. · Other. | 3.1, 4.1 |
| Q3 | The registration behaviours FBL would change (findings A9, B9, B10). | **(default) Keep the refusal for a bare file** (`createOnFirstPlacement: false`) **and adopt the rest**, which FBL gives no switch for: a stale position is pruned, a renamed resource keeps its position, a `language:` header may stand anywhere, a missing body is reported. Each is named in the transcript's diff. · **Adopt all**: the first drag of a bare file creates its registration. · Other. | 6.2, 6.3, 7.3 |
| Q4 | A sibling reading's menu entries and rows under another reading (finding A7). | **(default) Each reading offers its own**, as the remark in `RdfSelection.cs` intended; the entries that go are listed from the transcript. · **Keep them**, which stays module code until gap 7 is answered. · Other. | 4.3 |
| Q5 | Gaps 1 and 2 block writing through `plan`. What happens meanwhile? | **(default) Two stages**: reading and derivation are converted now, and commands keep writing through `RdfWriter` and `ShaclWriter` until FBL answers; the writers are then named in the companion notes as standing in for the gaps. · **Wait** for FBL before anything is built. · **Work around**: a host-private call hands the plugin the whole transaction. · Other. | 5.1 |
| Q6 | Are the four client canvases in scope? | **(default) Yes, one reading at a time, the RDF graph first**, each compiled with `compileNotation` and its hand-written definition kept as the oracle. · **No**: backend only. · Other. | 11 |

## Alignment with Product Vision

The product direction (2026-09-26) is one definition per tool, interpreted by a core in each IDE, with code only where a definition cannot reach. This module is the hardest test of that sentence in the repository: the largest, four tool types over one file, and the format both specifications name as their example of what stays code. DISL 4.11 was written with this tool as its example, and no host has run it. What the conversion finds is owed to etalii.adp before three other hosts build the same plugin.

## Requirements

### Requirement 1: An oracle before any change

**User Story:** As the owner of the tool, I want what it answers today frozen before anything is converted.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the work starts THEN one parity transcript per reading SHALL be generated from today's code and committed before any provider, projection or writer is changed, in the shape of the timeline's: per document the context menu of every element, of the empty canvas, of a placement, of a connect gesture and of an unknown id; the property rows; the findings; the payload of every mapped element; and a scripted edit sequence with each step's answer and the hunks it made.
2. The corpus SHALL be the module's examples, the copies under `src/examples/diagrams/rdf/`, the nine fixtures, and **one new fixture for each finding marked Read** in tables A and B, a file that starts with a byte-order mark among them.
3. A test SHALL require today's code to reproduce each transcript byte for byte, and SHALL have been seen to fail against a deliberately changed sentence first.
4. WHEN a later step changes a transcript THEN the change SHALL be one this document names (Q1, Q3, Q4), regenerated on purpose and reviewed as a diff. Any other difference is a regression.

### Requirement 2: Four definitions at DISL 0.3, bundled

**User Story:** As a tool engineer, I want one definition per tool type that every host runs.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. The four definitions in etalii-adp/etalii.adp SHALL be rewritten at DISL 0.3 with the constructs finding A3 names, and SHALL validate against the DISL schema there.
2. The stored types the four share SHALL be declared once and reused (finding A3, `imports`), or, IF the design shows that cannot be done, repeated identically and held equal by a test.
3. Each definition SHALL declare `persistence.format` `fbl` with the module's binding (Requirement 7.1), the plugin with `provides` including `persistenceFormat` and its `plans`, the id rules of Requirement 6.1, and its own `x-` block of wire ids (finding A6).
4. `specifications/disl/rdf-graph.dis` SHALL be brought in line with the rewritten `w3c-rdf.dis` or the difference recorded (finding A2), and the four companion notes rewritten to list only what DISL 0.3 cannot express.
5. The definitions SHALL be bundled into `src/diagrams/rdf/definition/` by `bundle-disl.sh`, never edited here, embedded, held by a `BundledDefinition.Tests`, and SHALL load with no diagnostic of severity error.

### Requirement 3: The body is read by the plugin

**User Story:** As a user, I want every `.ttl` and `.nt` that opens today to open the same.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. A persistence plugin with the id `net.etalii.adp.w3c.turtle` SHALL implement `read` over `RdfTokenizer` and `RdfParser`, delivering the stored elements of Q2, each with its entry's span and the span of every value it alone owns, as UTF-8 byte ranges (finding B5).
2. Reading SHALL never throw on content. A body that does not parse SHALL open empty and read-only with the one finding `rdf.unparseable`, today's sentence and the parser's line, under every reading.
3. `read` SHALL report the five `rdf.*` findings and no finding of a sibling reading (finding B15), each with today's code, severity, sentence and line.
4. A value written once for several elements (finding B3) SHALL be delivered so that no two elements claim one span as their own, and what the contract cannot express of it SHALL be recorded under Requirement 10.
5. `read` and `plan` SHALL be deterministic and SHALL NOT read the registration, the file system or the clock.

### Requirement 4: Each reading is derived

**User Story:** As a maintainer, I want every reading's elements, palette, menus, rows and findings to come from its definition.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. The drawn elements of each reading SHALL be the definition's derived elements over the stored model (Q2), and SHALL equal what the reading's projection yields today for every document of the corpus: ids, order, attributes and payloads.
2. The toolbox, the context menus, the property rows, the confirmations and the reason on every unavailable entry SHALL be derived through `ToolboxDerivation`, `ContextMenuDerivation` and `FormDerivation`, mapped to the wire ids of each `x-` block.
3. Each reading SHALL offer its own entries and rows (Q4), and the entries that no longer appear under another reading SHALL be listed in the transcript's diff.
4. Every sentence a user reads today SHALL be read unchanged: the truncation sentence on every withheld edit and read-only row, "Remove (with 3 statements)", the five sentences of a typed term that names nothing, the read-only reasons of the IRI, Types and Predicate rows, and the blank-node sentences.
5. The design SHALL list, per reading, each element kind, attribute and finding beside the construct that derives it or the plugin function that supplies it (finding A4), and SHALL measure the load of the two largest examples against `limits.celCost` before a reading is switched over (finding A10).
6. The twenty-three findings SHALL keep their codes, severities, sentences, lines and order, and no finding the tool does not give today SHALL appear.
7. The hand-written projections and providers SHALL be kept in the test project as the oracle and removed from the product code, reading by reading.

### Requirement 5: Every edit is planned as splices

**User Story:** As a user editing a file other tools own, I want an edit to change what I changed and nothing beside it.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN FBL has answered gaps 1 and 2 (Q5) THEN every command of the module SHALL write through the plugin's `plan`, and no command SHALL call a writer directly. UNTIL then the commands SHALL keep their writers, unchanged, behind the same store.
2. One gesture SHALL be one edit and one undo step, whatever number of triples it adds or removes.
3. The bytes an edit writes SHALL be today's, except as Q1 rules.
4. Every refusal SHALL keep today's sentence, the two blank-node sentences and the five of `ShaclRefusals` among them, and a refused edit SHALL leave the body untouched to the byte.
5. Adding a triple to an `.nt` body SHALL write N-Triples (finding B7), with a test seen to fail against today's writer first.
6. A document ADP did not change SHALL be written back byte-identical, for the line-ending fixtures and the one without a final newline too, and undo SHALL restore the body byte for byte.

### Requirement 6: Ids, positions and the registration

**User Story:** As an author who arranged a graph, I want it to open where I left it.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. Element ids SHALL be stated by the definitions and computed by no module code: `res:` and the IRI; `blank:` and the ordinal, ephemeral, with today's sentence as its reason; an edge's three parts joined by `|` with the repeat counter; OWL's `expr:`, `ind:`, `thing:` and `dt:` shapes; SHACL's `shacl-edge:`.
2. Every one of the 48 stored positions SHALL be applied after the conversion with no registration rewritten to make it so.
3. A bare file SHALL refuse a move with today's sentence, and the other registration behaviours SHALL be FBL's (Q3), each shown by a fixture.
4. A move SHALL write only the registration, as one undo step that restores it byte for byte.

### Requirement 7: Four readings of one body, routing and templates

**User Story:** As a user with one file open as a graph and as an ontology, I want an edit in one to show in the other.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. The module SHALL own its binding, `backend/EtAlii.Adp.Diagram.Rdf/w3c-turtle.fbl`, embedded; the example in etalii.adp SHALL be brought in line with it or the difference recorded.
2. The four readings SHALL share one open body, one model and one history, and an undo in any reading SHALL undo the body's most recent edit.
3. A bare `.ttl` or `.nt` SHALL open as `w3c/rdf`, the siblings SHALL be offered where today's markers match, in today's order (finding B12), and the SKOS reading SHALL draw the label its `language` header asks for; WHERE neither language can carry the header to the definition (finding A8) THEN module code SHALL supply it and be named as standing in for the gap.
4. A new document of each origin SHALL be the bytes its factory writes today (finding B8), from `template.byOrigin`, and SHALL read through the binding with no finding of severity warning or above.

### Requirement 8: What stays code, and why

**User Story:** As a maintainer, I want what remains to be what the languages cannot state.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. The module SHALL keep the tokenizer, the parser and the writers behind the plugin; the layouts; the element mappers and the viewport filter; the store; the `.proto` payloads; and the plugin's CEL functions.
2. The four projections, the four validators' reading-specific rules and the logic of the providers SHALL leave the product code as each reading is switched over.
3. WHEN the conversion is complete THEN each companion note SHALL list every remaining class beside the gap or the host concern that keeps it, and a class with neither SHALL be removed.

### Requirement 9: The library work this module needs

**User Story:** As a maintainer of the shared libraries, I want each thing added once, for every tool.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. `EtAlii.Adp.Specification.Disl` SHALL implement derived node types (4.11.2), budgets (3.2.1), `ephemeral` id rules (11.5.3), `imports` if Requirement 2.2 uses them, and the graph functions of 12.4 the definitions call (finding A5), each proven by a library test seen to fail first.
2. `EtAlii.Adp.Specification.Fbl` SHALL let a tool give the sentence of an unreadable plugin body (finding B14), and SHALL group the changes of one gesture into one history entry (finding B1).
3. No module name SHALL appear in a library change, and a language gap SHALL NOT be repaired here.

### Requirement 10: Gaps are recorded and reported, never tuned away

**User Story:** As the owner of DISL and FBL, I want every place they fall short reported with its evidence.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. Each language gap of section C, and any the implementation adds, SHALL be recorded in the companion notes with the construct concerned, the fixture that shows it, and what would resolve it.
2. A gap SHALL NOT be closed by weakening a check, skipping a fixture, or stating in a definition something the tool does not do.
3. WHEN a *read* finding turns out not to occur THEN it SHALL be struck here with the fixture that shows it, as a small amendment.
4. The delivery report SHALL list every gap as a candidate change for etalii-adp/etalii.adp and every definition defect repaired.

### Requirement 11: The client

**User Story:** As a user, I want each canvas to look and behave as it does, drawn from the definition the backend runs.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. Each canvas definition SHALL be compiled from its bundled definition with `parseDisl` and `compileNotation` (Q6), the RDF graph first, with today's hand-written definition kept in a test as the oracle.
2. IF `compileNotation` cannot read something a definition states THEN it SHALL be added to the shared library, named for its geometry, and SHALL NOT be written in this module.
3. A `tests.md` entry per reading SHALL cover in a real browser, in both themes: the cards, rows and badges of an example, a blank card, the truncation banner on `laureates.ttl` with its withheld menu, each toolbox drop, a relation drawn between two cards, a move with its undo, and the same file open under two readings showing one edit in both.

### Requirement 12: Documentation, catalog and gates

**User Story:** As a reader of the repository, I want its pages to stay true.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. `src/diagrams/readme.md`, `docs/creating-a-diagram-module.md`, `docs/architecture.md` and `docs/solution-structure.md` SHALL be updated in the change that makes a sentence of theirs false, and the four rows of `docs/tools.md` SHALL name this specification.
2. All four gates SHALL exit zero on every pull request of this specification, judged by captured exit codes, with a newly created worktree built before a green gate is trusted about the bundled definitions.
3. WHEN the tasks document is written THEN every acceptance criterion here SHALL be claimed by a task, established by diffing the two sets, and two traces SHALL be read back to their artefacts.

## Non-Functional Requirements

### Code Architecture and Modularity

- The module ends as four definitions, one binding, one plugin and the code Requirement 8.1 names. The house rules of `src/.editorconfig` and the three rules the gates refuse apply. `.ttl` and `.nt` are byte-compared and already `-text`; `.dis` and `.fbl` follow what the hype cycle's have.

### Performance

- Opening, validating and editing the largest example SHALL not be perceptibly slower than today (Requirement 4.5). The drawn-element budget stays 1,000 cards and the viewport filter stays.

### Reliability

- No file that opens today opens differently. No stored position is lost. An unchanged document is written back byte-identical. Undo restores bytes. Every test written for a finding is seen to fail against it first.

### Usability

- Every sentence a user reads today is read unchanged, unless this document names the change.

## Out of scope

- Any change to what the four tools do beyond the six questions and finding B7.
- Changing DISL or FBL. The gaps are reported; a language change is etalii.adp's own specification.
- Declaring Turtle as an FBL family. FBL 11.5 expects it to stay a plugin, and this document does not argue otherwise.
- The SPARQL tool, which shares the `w3c` vendor and nothing else, and the other tools of the series.

## Appendix: the binding, as drafted

A draft against FBL 0.2. It differs from the example in etalii.adp where findings B8, B9 and B12 say so: the templates are the four factories' bytes, a bare file gets no registration from a drag, and the origins are in today's order. `"name": true` in `reader.receives` is **not valid FBL 0.2**: it marks where the construct of finding B7 and gap 5 is needed. `{local}` is **not a placeholder of FBL 13**: it stands for the factories' own folding of the base name, which `{key}` does not reproduce (finding B8).

```json
{
  "fbl": "0.2",
  "bindings": {
    "turtle": {
      "title": "RDF in Turtle or N-Triples",
      "claims": {
        "extensions": [".ttl", ".nt"],
        "origins": ["w3c/rdf", "w3c/owl", "w3c/skos", "w3c/shacl"],
        "readings": {
          "w3c/rdf": { "bare": true },
          "w3c/owl": { "suggest": { "contains": ["owl:Ontology", "http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#Ontology"] } },
          "w3c/skos": { "suggest": { "contains": ["skos:ConceptScheme", "http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#ConceptScheme"] } },
          "w3c/shacl": { "suggest": { "contains": ["sh:NodeShape", "sh:property", "http://www.w3.org/ns/shacl#NodeShape"] } }
        }
      },
      "body": { "kind": "file" },
      "reader": { "plugin": "net.etalii.adp.w3c.turtle", "version": "^0.1.0", "receives": { "name": true } },
      "text": { "newline": "crlf", "indent": 4, "finalNewline": true },
      "registration": {
        "headers": { "language": { "doc": "w3c/skos: the BCP 47 tag whose skos:prefLabel is shown, such as 'de'." } },
        "createOnFirstPlacement": false
      },
      "template": {
        "text": "@prefix ex: <http://example.org/> .\r\n@prefix rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#> .\r\n\r\nex:{local} a ex:Resource ;\r\n    rdfs:label \"{base}\" .\r\n",
        "byOrigin": {
          "w3c/owl": "@prefix : <http://example.org/{local}#> .\r\n@prefix owl: <http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#> .\r\n@prefix rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#> .\r\n\r\n<http://example.org/{local}> a owl:Ontology ;\r\n    rdfs:label \"{base}\" .\r\n\r\n:Thing1 a owl:Class ;\r\n    rdfs:label \"First class\" .\r\n",
          "w3c/skos": "@prefix skos: <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#> .\r\n@prefix ex: <http://example.org/> .\r\n\r\nex:{local} a skos:ConceptScheme ;\r\n    skos:prefLabel \"{base}\"@en ;\r\n    skos:hasTopConcept ex:{local}_top .\r\n\r\nex:{local}_top a skos:Concept ;\r\n    skos:prefLabel \"Top concept\"@en ;\r\n    skos:topConceptOf ex:{local} .\r\n",
          "w3c/shacl": "@prefix sh: <http://www.w3.org/ns/shacl#> .\r\n@prefix xsd: <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#> .\r\n@prefix ex: <http://example.org/> .\r\n\r\nex:{local}Shape a sh:NodeShape ;\r\n    sh:targetClass ex:{local} ;\r\n    sh:name \"{base}\" ;\r\n    sh:property [\r\n        sh:path ex:name ;\r\n        sh:datatype xsd:string ;\r\n        sh:minCount 1 ;\r\n        sh:maxCount 1 ;\r\n    ] .\r\n"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The design closes `{local}` one of three ways: the plugin's `template` operation, which FBL asks only when the binding has no `template.text`; `{key}`, with the changed local names of a new document named in the transcript; or a report that `{key}` cannot keep a hyphen.

## Appendix: the definitions' persistence and wire ids, as drafted

The block below is `w3c-rdf.dis`; the three siblings carry the same `persistence` and `plugins` with their own derived types and their own `x-` block. The rest of each definition is the design's (Requirement 4.5). `Triple`, `Prefix` and `Base` are the stored types of Q2, named as the plugin delivers them, so no `typeMap` is needed.

```json
{
  "persistence": {
    "format": "fbl",
    "binding": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etalii-adp/etalii.adp.ide.standalone/develop/src/diagrams/rdf/backend/EtAlii.Adp.Diagram.Rdf/w3c-turtle.fbl#turtle",
    "ids": {
      "strategy": "natural", "stable": false,
      "pattern": "^(res:.+|blank:[0-9]+|edge:.+|triple:.+|prefix:.*|base|truncation)$",
      "types": {
        "Triple": { "strategy": "derived", "expression": "'triple:' + self.s + '|' + self.p + '|' + self.o + repeatSuffix(self)", "ephemeral": { "cel": "self.sKind == 'blank' || self.oKind == 'blank'" } },
        "Prefix": { "strategy": "derived", "expression": "'prefix:' + self.name + repeatSuffix(self)" },
        "Base": { "strategy": "derived", "expression": "'base'" },
        "BlankNode": { "ephemeral": true, "reason": "That is a blank node, whose identity does not survive a reparse, so a stored position could not be trusted. Name it with an IRI to arrange it." }
      }
    },
    "view": { "store": ["bounds"], "styleOverrides": "none" }
  },
  "viewpoints": { "graph": { "label": "Graph", "exclude": ["Triple", "Prefix", "Base"], "default": true } },
  "plugins": {
    "net.etalii.adp.w3c.turtle": {
      "version": "^0.1.0", "required": true,
      "provides": ["persistenceFormat", "celFunctions"],
      "plans": ["add", "set", "remove"]
    }
  },
  "x-rdf": {
    "tools": {
      "resource": { "id": "rdf.toolbox.resource", "drop": "rdf.add-resource" },
      "prefix": { "id": "rdf.toolbox.prefix", "drop": "rdf.add-prefix" }
    },
    "actions": {
      "addResource": "rdf.add-resource",
      "declarePrefix": "rdf.add-prefix",
      "relate": "rdf.connect",
      "renameResource": "rdf.rename-resource",
      "removeResource": "rdf.remove-resource",
      "removeStatement": "rdf.remove-edge"
    },
    "properties": {
      "iri": "rdf.iri",
      "types": "rdf.types",
      "label": "rdf.label",
      "comment": "rdf.comment",
      "predicateIri": "rdf.predicate"
    }
  }
}
```

`repeatSuffix` stands for the repeat counter of DISL 11.5.2, written out there with `positionIn`; it is the quadratic rule of finding A10. A `Prefix` stored type is not in `rdf-graph.dis`, which reaches prefixes only through plugin functions; it is here because `rdf.duplicate-prefix` is a finding about declarations and Declare prefix adds one.
